steps.what: Determine diagnostic test indication and patient-specific precautions
Administer or order the selected diagnostic tests within authorised scope
outputs: administered test or confirmed test request

tasks.design: Retain diagnostic selection and the applicable administration or ordering action with an authorised practitioner. The {OTHER} clinical ordering system supports requests; no reduction in physical procedures or clinical choice is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test indications, precautions and scope depend on the patient and care setting.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order screens support the retained action; the digest provides no test-administration saving.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing appropriate tests and recognising contraindications.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret the presentation and take responsibility for the test action.
tasks.altitude: Clinical authority and procedure time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Match clinical questions to safe test preparation

evidence.claim: Diagnostic test selection and physical administration are not replaced by the digest's note-drafting capabilities.

assumptions: Boundary is physician assistant selection and the applicable administration or ordering route, not both as compulsory sequential work; diagnostic-team execution after referral is excluded.
Practitioner produces the test decision in s1 with time fully retained; no structured indication or machine request is assumed.
National rules and local delegation determine authorised scope and any supervising approval; existing required supervision is unchanged.
Check native ordering tools first. No new workflow adds upkeep.
research_questions: Which part of test ordering is genuinely repeated entry rather than clinical selection or preparation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+70=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Clinical selection and the applicable physical or ordering route retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel patients about care and health

steps.what: Instruct and counsel patients about therapeutic regimens and health concerns

tasks.design: Retain personal counselling and understanding checks. Vetted {DOCS} patient information supports explanations without assuming a separate drafting baseline or shorter emotional-support conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice must fit the patient's understanding, concerns and treatment context.
tasks.enabler_now: Guideline-based patient information is available as supporting material.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive topics, distress and misunderstandings about treatment.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, notice concerns and adapt the conversation.
tasks.altitude: Patient-facing counselling time and responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Use consistent explanations and escalation advice

evidence.claim: Thuisarts provides guideline-based patient information; this supports a reference source rather than replacing individual counselling.

assumptions: Boundary is physician assistant counselling, excluding treatment selection and patient self-care.
The treating practitioner produces the prescribed regimen under existing care processes; no automated personal advice or structured regimen extraction is assumed.
Use native access to vetted information first. No new counselling workflow means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Can the patient explain how the regimen applies to their own situation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Supporting information does not itself reduce counselling, emotional support or understanding checks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review patients and update the care team

steps.what: Visit and observe patients during rounds or house calls
Update charts with checked visit findings

loop.purpose: Draft chart wording from visit findings
loop.input: Consented visit account or practitioner dictation and relevant prior chart
loop.output: Draft chart update with uncertain facts marked
loop.check: Practitioner checks symptoms, examination findings, negation, chronology, attribution and omissions against the visit account
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported or ambiguous facts return to manual charting
loop.why_not_simpler: Clinical narrative meaning cannot be preserved by fixed field copying alone

steps.what: Assess and order indicated therapy within authorised scope
Report visit findings and therapy decisions to the physician

tasks.design: Use a bounded chart draft inside the {OTHER} clinical record system, checked and confirmed by the physician assistant. Keep patient visits, clinical therapy decisions and physician handover intact; the draft does not place therapy orders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative chart wording adds documentation work after the clinical visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Consultation-note drafting with clinician validation exists today.
tasks.still_hard: Faithful charting and clinical escalation when findings change the care plan.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the patient and explain clinical concerns to the physician.
tasks.altitude: Less initial chart wording, with unchanged clinical and supervisory boundaries.

reach.learn: Trace every chart claim to a visit source

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation records for clinician validation and clinical record systems.
A 40% reduction in the chart-wording component is an unmeasured scenario, not a reduction in rounds or clinical decisions.

assumptions: Boundary includes physician assistant visit, charting, therapy decisions and handover; physician time is excluded and unchanged. Allocate any overlap with test ordering or other documentation tasks once.

Practitioner produces findings during s1, including symptoms, examination observations, source attribution and chronology. Capture and clarification remain within its full 45 hours; without permitted recording use counted dictation or manual charting.
Test native templates and dictation first. No model-produced clinical order is enabled.
National rules and local delegation define therapy-order authority and escalation. The unchanged supervisory process remains required.
Three additional focal hours cover source samples, template changes and exceptional draft failures.
research_questions: Does chart drafting reduce net documentation effort while preserving clinical meaning and handover quality?

already_counted.description: Chart draft review, correction and confirmation

incremental.description: Source samples, template upkeep and failed draft handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact chart text, patient identity, date and source attribution; edits require renewed practitioner confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+15+15+15=90, gross=10, upkeep=3, net=7. High assumes a 40% reduction in the 25-hour charting component only; low retains manual charting for difficult accounts plus upkeep. Visit, therapy and physician reporting time never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Supervise and coordinate technicians and technical assistants during care delivery

tasks.design: Keep direct technical supervision and clinical coordination with the practitioner. Existing {DOCS} procedures support the work; no separate rota administration or employee scoring system is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe allocation and correction depend on competence and live care conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated replacement for direct supervision is supplied in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe work and changing priorities quickly.
tasks.human_edge: Coach staff and intervene when supervision is needed.
tasks.altitude: Supervisory authority and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Live technical supervision remains human work; the digest does not establish a supervisory labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is physician assistant supervision, excluding technician execution and separate service scheduling.
Practitioner observes performance and workload during counted supervision; no structured competence flags or machine allocation are assumed.
Use native procedure access first. Unchanged supervision adds zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which technical activities require immediate practitioner supervision?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Live supervision and coordination retain all practitioner effort; staff execution time is excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Chart wording may take less time; diagnostic choices, counselling, visits, therapy decisions and supervision remain within existing professional authority.
reach: Improve chart traceability with medical records specialists
Coordinate clinical supervision with registered nurses
role.ambitious_version: A physician assistant with less repetitive chart composition who retains patient assessment, clinical responsibility and direct team communication.
